$comment: Prop scatter and batching. Every number the Meadows looks like lives here; PropBatcher.ts and Prototypes.ts contain no tuning literals. Moving this into a per-biome file is the M6 job, when a second biome exists to justify the schema.
$comment_batching: Props are batched by (family x spatial cell), NOT by terrain chunk. Per-chunk batching cost one draw call per chunk per family and measured 1576 draw calls against a budget of 150. A cell is sized to its family's own draw distance, so at most 3x3 cells of any family are ever resident and each is one draw call.
$comment_cellSize: cellSize == drawDistance is deliberate. The disc of radius R around the player reaches at most one cell in each direction when cells are R across, capping resident cells per family at 9 before distance culling. Larger cells mean fewer draws but more wasted instances behind the player; smaller cells invert that.

families.$comment: Sparse oak groves in grassland, GAME_DESIGN.md section 9. The meadow gets the occasional lone tree, the grove gets a stand.
Kept as its own family so groves mix silhouettes.

The densest family by an order of magnitude, so it still gets the shortest draw distance. It used to stop at 44m against a 384m terrain view, which is why the meadow read as a bare golf course; the leaf-tuft source (36 tris, was 224) bought the range back at a third of the old triangle cost (D51).
